_comment: Guided tour of AI Settings (Qt tool and emtk app). Steps point at real controls and wait for the user to press them. 'name' is the emtk control (a field's attr, a button's action); 'attr'/'action' are what the Qt tool resolves.

steps.title: Pick a provider
steps.text: Every provider keeps its own endpoint, key and models, so switching here never carries your key across. The list is ordered by where your data goes: Mistral (EU) first, then Local — Ollama or LM Studio on your own machine, where nothing leaves the computer at all.

steps.title: The key, and where it lives
steps.text:
Paste a key and it is saved and tested immediately (press Enter, or click elsewhere). It is drawn as stars; the Show key check box (the eye in the Qt window) shows it in clear text for this session only. It goes into ai_api_settings.json in your settings directory, written so only your account can read it.

If you already export MISTRAL_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY in your shell, you can leave this empty — ChiSurf finds it.

steps.title: Ask the provider what it has
steps.text: Fetch models reads the provider's model list in the background and sorts it into text-capable and image-capable, filling the pick lists below the two model fields. Press it now.

steps.title: Two models, two jobs
steps.text: The text model drives the code editor's agent panel and AI curve triage. The image model is used only to generate plugin icons. Type an id into either field if the provider does not advertise one you know works, or pick one from the fetched lists.

steps.title: Check it before you rely on it
steps.text: Test connection asks the endpoint for its model list, which tells you whether the URL is reachable and the key accepted. Note it does not verify the selected model itself can run.

await.hint: Press Test connection and watch the result line.

steps.title: Reset is safe
steps.text: Reset puts this provider's fields back to their defaults but does not write anything — press Save if you want to keep them, or switch providers to discard.
